name: Oberndorf in Tirol
kurzbeschreibung: Peaceful village between St. Johann and Kitzbühel, featuring a beautiful parish church and stunning Alpine views.
beschreibung:
Oberndorf in Tirol lies at an altitude of 684 metres in the Kitzbühel holiday region with the Kitzbüheler Alpen and is a tranquil village. The village has around 2,300 inhabitants and stretches over a spacious area with typical Tiroler farmhouses and agricultural farms.

Those seeking relaxation enjoy the peace and seclusion away from the tourist crowds, and the untouched nature around the village invites extended exploration, while hikers get their money's worth on numerous marked trails around the village. In the summer months (from May to October), the surroundings turn into an outdoor paradise.

Oberndorf in Tirol is particularly suitable for families and those seeking relaxation who want to combine peace and quiet with activities. The good transport connections and the proximity to larger towns make the stay especially pleasant.
text:
Overview

Oberndorf in Tirol is situated in the sunny Leuken Valley in the district of Kitzbühel at an altitude of 687 metres, nestled between the world-famous alpine sport town of Kitzbühel to the south and St. Johann in Tirol to the north. This vibrant municipality has around 2,400 residents and covers 17.7 square kilometres at the foot of the Kitzbüheler Horn and the craggy peaks of the Wilder Kaiser. Its location on the broad valley floor along the Kitzbüheler Ache river provides the village with plenty of sunshine and splendid 360-degree mountain panoramas. While the village centre has carefully preserved its traditional agricultural charm with flower-bedecked timber farmhouses, Oberndorf harmoniously combines rural tranquillity with state-of-the-art tourist amenities. Scattered hamlets and rolling moorland in Bichlach characterize the picturesque landscape rising into the Kitzbühel Alps.

History

Settlement in the Leuken Valley began during the Bronze Age, driven by early copper exploration. Oberndorf was first documented in written records during the 12th century. The village experienced an era of European prominence in the 16th century due to flourishing copper and silver mining on Mount Rerobichl. It was here that miners sank the legendary Heilig-Geist-Schacht (Holy Spirit Shaft), which reached an astonishing vertical depth of 886 metres, making it the deepest mineshaft in the known world at that time. Vast quantities of high-grade ore were extracted, bringing great prosperity to the region. By the 18th century, mining declined, and agriculture resumed its central role. A major cultural landmark is the late Baroque Parish Church of Saints Philip and James, erected between 1733 and 1734 by architect Jakob Singer, adorned with Wessobrunn stucco and altarpieces by Simon Benedikt Faistenberger.

Getting There

Oberndorf in Tirol boasts exceptional transport connections. By car, drivers arriving from Germany can travel toll-free via Kiefersfelden or Kufstein along federal roads B178 and B161 straight to Oberndorf. From Innsbruck or Salzburg, the Inntal Autobahn A12 connects via Wörgl into the Leuken Valley. Rail travellers enjoy their own station, Oberndorf in Tirol, located on the historic Gisela Railway (Salzburg-Tyrol line), served hourly by regional trains offering direct connections to Wörgl, Kitzbühel, and Salzburg. Nearby express railway hubs in St. Johann in Tirol and Kitzbühel offer direct links to international ICE and Railjet networks. In resort, frequent local buses and winter ski shuttles run seamlessly between the village core and the ski lift stations.

Tips

In winter, the 10-seater Bauernpenzing gondola lift is the star attraction, whisking skiers straight from the valley floor into the St. Johann in Tirol / Oberndorf ski area, featuring 42 kilometres of well-groomed slopes on the snowy northern flanks of the Kitzbüheler Horn. Another must-see is the historic Müllnerhof, an 800-year-old traditional farm estate that houses a private rural museum and the world's largest wooden fountain according to the Guinness Book of Records, carved out of a massive single tree trunk by Werner Thum. Nature enthusiasts will enjoy walking through the peaceful ponds and rolling hills of Bichlach or exploring the historic mining trail on Mount Rerobichl. In summer, the heated Oberndorf Panorama Open-Air Pool with giant water slides offers refreshing fun for the whole family.
